## Abstract

Random forests are commonly introduced as flexible predictive models,
but introductory applications often rely on default tuning parameters.
We investigate whether tuning meaningfully improves predictive performance
under a range of simulated data-generating conditions.

Using repeated cross-validation, we compare models that vary the number
of candidate variables considered at each split, minimum node size, and
number of trees. Our results show that tuning has relatively little impact
in some high-signal settings but can substantially improve performance
when signal is weaker or predictors contain substantial noise.

**Keywords:** random forest, machine learning, simulation, cross-validation
